clue.text: Boatman in part of the island

definitions.meaning: one of the three friends rowing up the Thames in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
the southern, mountainous half of Lewis and ..., the largest island of the Outer Hebrides off Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: Both are proper names: a character in Jerome's rowing novel and the southern portion of a Hebridean island famous for tweed.

clue.text: Of purely theoretical interest to the professor

definitions.meaning: irrelevant in practice, as in 'the point is moot'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both of no practical consequence and a university scholar.

clue.text: It hots things up in the cooler

definitions.text: It hots things up in the cooler

parts.words: It hots things up in the cooler
parts.note: suggests a heater in prison, the cooler, but a car's cooling device is what is meant, working by taking heat from the engine

explanation.definitionFit: A heating panel warms a room, and a car's engine cooler bears the same name.

clue.text: Wearing a vest — one in a suit

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
having clothes on

explanation.surface: Someone in just a vest, alone among men in suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in a suit' is from bridge: a card that is the only one of its suit in a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a lone card of a suit in a hand is so called.

clue.text: "Speech created thought, which is the measure of the —" (Shelley)

definitions.text: "Speech created thought, which is the measure of the —" (Shelley)

parts.words: "Speech created thought, which is the measure of the —" (Shelley)
parts.note: a line from Shelley's verse drama Prometheus Unbound with its final word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shelley with its last word missing, to be completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's line in Prometheus Unbound ends with the word for the whole cosmos, everything that exists.

clue.text: International body and state combine, with no strings

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations
condition means state, as in 'in good condition'
to ally is to join together

explanation.surface: The UN and a country uniting, with no conditions attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Without strings means without any conditions or reservations.

clue.text: Sport five song books

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
an aria is a solo song in opera
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sports anthology: five books of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is the biologist's word for a mutant plant or animal, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a sport is a mutant or a variation from the normal type.

clue.text: Distantly provide accommodation in Rye perhaps

indicators.note: in places the lodging word within the shuffled letters
perhaps indicates that the letters of Rye are a possible variant arrangement

parts.note: a motel offers accommodation

explanation.surface: Arranging lodging in the Sussex town of Rye, a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns RYE into REY, and 'in' puts MOTEL between E and Y. Rye is a small town in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away, at a great distance.

clue.text: Obtained by force out of wrong pressman

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of
a tort is a civil wrong in law
ED is short for editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: Got by force from a journalist who had done wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to wring money or a promise from someone by threats.

clue.text: Like one treating Ida with scorn

definitions.text: Like one treating Ida with scorn

indicators.note: treating suggests processing or working over material, so the letters of Ida and scorn are reworked

explanation.surface: Describing someone who is contemptuous towards a woman called Ida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' rearranges IDA plus SCORN; the whole clue is also the definition, since someone scornful is mocking and bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scornful person speaks with mocking, bitter contempt, which is the sneering tone this adjective names.

clue.text: Quick to help players

definitions.meaning: to supply forgotten lines to actors from the wings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both punctual and, as a verb, to feed a forgotten line to an actor on stage.

clue.text: Happened to be on the ground

parts.note: taken as written
something that has dropped to the floor has fallen

explanation.surface: Something that happened to end up lying on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participles of verbs meaning occurred, as in 'what has happened to him' or 'what has befallen him'.

clue.text: Publican with no end of trade

indicators.note: with no signals the removal of the following word from the publican synonym

parts.note: a publican serves drinks, as a bartender does

explanation.surface: A pub landlord whose trade never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes the letters END from BARTENDER, leaving the word for swapping goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To barter is to trade goods by exchange rather than for money.

clue.text: Dismissed side entirely

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
right is one side, as opposed to left

explanation.surface: A cricket team bowled out completely.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a dismissed batsman is OUT; the surface suggests a whole team ('side') being dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely and fully, as in 'he won outright'.

clue.text: Farmworker having the sense to be wise with this

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A farmhand with the good sense to be wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hind' as a farmhand is an old Scottish and northern usage; the definition plays on 'being wise after the event'.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone is wise after the event, when looking back on it.

clue.text: Cliff, mark,…

definitions.meaning: a steep rocky crag or cliff face, a northern English word
a lasting trace left on skin by a healed wound

explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots lead on to the next clue, 17 across, as if one sentence continued; they are only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a steep rocky outcrop in northern England and the mark a healed wound leaves.

clue.text: Was not Macbeth's dagger, he asked, — to feeling as to sight?

definitions.text: Was not Macbeth's dagger, he asked, — to feeling as to sight?

parts.words: Was not Macbeth's dagger, he asked, — to feeling as to sight?
parts.note: recalls Macbeth's speech 'Is this a dagger which I see before me', asking whether the vision could be touched as well as seen, with the key word left blank

explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth asks if the dagger is perceptible to touch, using the old sense of a word now meaning level-headed.

clue.text: A claret with a new sort of menu

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Ordering a claret from a new style of menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes priced individually rather than as a set meal, from French for 'by the card'.

clue.text: . was an explorer, by the way

parts.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone who was an explorer, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Byrd was the American admiral who explored Antarctica by air; the leading dots carry on from 15 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Byrd, the American naval aviator, led polar expeditions to Antarctica.

clue.text: Clasp made by better artist

indicators.note: made suggests something constructed from raw materials, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A clasp crafted by a superior artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges BETTER together with RA (Royal Academician).
explanation.definitionFit: A hair slide or clip that fastens hair in place.

clue.text: Soldiers lead when, for example, others get up and come out again

indicators.note: lead says the soldiers' abbreviation comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: get up in a down clue means the pieces rise, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: EG, short for exempli gratia
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, other soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers take the lead when others rise and step out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' turns EG + REME into EMERGE in this down clue; RE and REME are British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface once more after disappearing.

clue.text: In balance, for instance, one with a means of recognition

parts.note: taken as written
the Balance, Libra, is a sign of the zodiac
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Weighing things up, a person with a way of being identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' here is Libra, one of the zodiac signs, not a weighing scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Badges and emblems identify rank or membership, which is exactly what insignia do.

clue.text: A tendency not to move in rate revision without one

indicators.note: without means outside, so the shuffled letters go round the single letter
revision suggests reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A reluctance to change a rate when revising it without anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges IN + RATE to INERTA, and 'without' (outside) puts that around I.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, the property of resisting any change in motion; figuratively, sluggishness.

clue.text: 'ow to beat one's wife, say, at this game?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, here in a Cockney voice that drops the h

parts.note: to hit her, to sock her, which a Cockney would pronounce without the h

explanation.surface: A rough Cockney joke about hitting one's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: ''ow' for 'how' shows the speaker drops initial h, so 'sock her' becomes 'sock 'er', which is pronounced like the football game.
explanation.definitionFit: Association football is the game, the name formed from 'Association'.

clue.text: Cures, with prohibition of careless play

parts.note: a no is a refusal or ban
strumming a guitar is playing it casually

explanation.surface: Remedies, along with a ban on sloppy playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Quack remedies or pet panaceas, claimed to fix ailments.

clue.text: Scold worker about to desert

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a worker bee
to rat on is to desert or betray

explanation.surface: Telling off an employee who is about to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does not mean 'on the point of'; it puts BEE around RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate is to tell off or rebuke angrily.

clue.text: Bond uses decoy to surround one gun

indicators.note: to surround signals that the decoy word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a lure draws prey into a trap
the Roman numeral for one is I
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: James Bond uses a decoy to trap a gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests James Bond, but it is the definition: a tie or binding.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is anything that ties or binds, such as a cord or surgical thread.

clue.text: Refinement can perhaps appear in a threnody

indicators.note: appear in signals that the shuffled word goes inside the lament

parts.note: a threnody is a song of mourning, an elegy

indicators.note: perhaps indicates that the letters of can are a possible variant arrangement

explanation.surface: Grace and polish showing through in a funeral lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CAN to ANC, which 'appear in' puts inside ELEGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance and polish of style, an older form of the familiar word.

clue.text: Worn the other way round by Labour man in rows?

indicators.note: the other way round means the two pieces go in the opposite order to the expected phrase

parts.note: a tie is an item worn round the neck
a red is a left-winger, as Labour supporters are often called

explanation.surface: A Labour politician wears his red tie, but the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: A Labour man would wear a RED TIE; 'the other way round' swaps the words to TIE RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats arranged in tiers rise in successive rows, as in a theatre.
